title: Check yourself: after the votes, and while the session waits

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A participant marks the cardholder's discount voucher as redeemed in prepare and returns PREPARED | NO_JOIN. A participant after it declines the purchase with 51. What becomes of the voucher?

options.text: It is free again, since a participant that did not join still gets abort when a later one declines
options.says: NO_JOIN means no abort call: only participants that joined hear the outcome

options.text: It stays redeemed, since a participant that did not join gets neither a commit nor an abort call
options.says: NO_JOIN means no commit and no abort call, so nothing undoes what prepare changed outside the Context

options.text: It is free again, since the TransactionManager undoes what a participant that did not join changed
options.says: the TransactionManager knows nothing about what a participant changed; only that participant's abort can undo it

options.text: It stays redeemed, since a participant that did not join is told only when a purchase commits
options.says: a participant that did not join gets no commit call either; it hears neither outcome

origin.section: 4.2 A Participant Hears the Outcome Only If It Joined

questions.stem: An audit participant joins every transaction and writes one row in commit and one in abort. It is declared after the PIN check, which votes ABORTED on a wrong PIN, and it implements only TransactionParticipant. After a morning with forty wrong PINs, how many audit rows describe them?

options.text: None of them, since after the ABORTED vote the audit participant is never prepared and never joins
options.says: after an abort only AbortParticipants are offered prepareForAbort; a plain participant later in the chain never joins, so its abort is never called

options.text: None of them, since abort is called only when a commit has failed on one of the participants
options.says: abort is the other outcome of the votes, not a reaction to a failed commit; a failed commit is only logged

options.text: All forty, since abort is called on every participant in the chain once the transaction aborts
options.says: abort goes only to participants that joined, and a plain participant after the abort never got the chance to join

options.text: All forty, since prepare runs on every participant before the TransactionManager counts the votes
options.says: the votes are not collected first: once one participant votes ABORTED, plain participants after it are skipped

origin.section: 4.3 After an Abort, Only Abort Participants Are Asked

questions.stem: Every participant votes PREPARED on a purchase of 18.40. Then the participant that credits loyalty points calls the points service in its commit, the service is down, and the call throws. SendResponse is declared last. What does the terminal receive?

options.text: A decline, since the exception turns the transaction into an abort and SendResponse sends the abort answer
options.says: once every participant has voted PREPARED there is no way back; an exception in commit is only a warning

options.text: No answer, since the exception ends the round of commit calls before SendResponse is reached
options.says: the TransactionManager logs the exception and calls the next participant's commit

options.text: The approval, since SendResponse sent the response in its prepare, before any commit ran
options.says: SendResponse sends in its commit or abort, as the 4.4 trace shows: it answered after RecordApproval's commit failed

options.text: The approval, since the exception is logged as a warning and SendResponse's commit still runs
options.says: commit cannot change the outcome: the warning is logged, the next commit runs, and the approval goes out without the points

questions.stem: A TransactionManager runs ten sessions, and its participant waits for a host that takes 500 ms per request. Requests arrive at 30 a second, all day, and IncomingListener's timeout is 15 seconds. What do terminals see after the first few minutes?

options.text: Answers in about half a second, since ten sessions at 500 ms each can take all 30 a second
options.says: each session is held for the whole 500 ms, so ten of them finish only 20 transactions a second

options.text: Answers in about half a second, since ten sessions hand their 500 ms waits to the host's threads
options.says: a blocking call holds the session's own thread for as long as the host takes

options.text: Waits that grow, then requests that expire, since ten sessions at 500 ms each finish 20 a second
options.says: throughput is sessions over the time each transaction holds one; 30 a second against 20 grows the queue until the listener's timeout drops Contexts

options.text: Waits that grow, then requests that expire, since IncomingListener holds each request 15 s first
options.says: IncomingListener queues the Context at once; its timeout is how long the Context may wait in the queue, and the queue grows because ten sessions held 500 ms each finish only 20 a second

origin.section: 4.6 A Session Is Busy for the Whole Transaction

concepts: An exception in commit is logged as a warning and the next participant's commit still runs, so the approval goes out; what can fail belongs in prepare.
A participant that reserves in prepare and votes NO_JOIN is never told of a later decline, so the reservation is never given back.
After an ABORTED vote plain participants later in the chain are never prepared and never hear the abort; an AbortParticipant is offered prepareForAbort, which calls prepare by default.
A session is held for the whole transaction, so throughput is sessions over time per transaction; past it the queue grows until the listener's timeout drops requests.
